title: SteleKit sketch sheet, schema 2
description: The native scene file at <graph>/assets/stelekit-sketch/<slug>/sheets/<sheetUuid>.v2.json. Units: 1 scene unit = 1/16 inch; x grows right, y grows down. This schema checks shape and types; the byte-exact canonical form (key order, number text) is produced by `sketch-cli canonicalize`, not by this schema. Spec: docs/reference/sketch-format-v2.md.

sheetUuid.description: UUID of the sheet; also the file name stem.

elements.description: In paint order: later entries draw on top (within a layer, ordered by z).

extras.description: Sheet-level keys the app does not interpret are kept as written. Known: sheetKind = "technical"; dimensionsOn = true|false (optional: whether the sheet shows dimension annotations; absent means on for a technical sheet, off for a diagram); agent = {mode, title, spec} written by `sketch-cli build`; sheetSetup = the print setup (paper, drawing scale, title block; see $defs/sheetSetup), written only once someone sets one.

layers.description: The layer "default" always exists; it is added when absent.

nameCounters.description: Highest auto-name ordinal issued per kind (rectangle, line, arrow, text, ...).

sw.description: Stroke width in scene units. On a real-world plan 16 = 1 inch.

rough.description: 0 = clean lines; higher = hand-drawn wobble when drawn in Sketchy style.

id.description: Id of the bound shape (not an arrow, not the arrow itself).

fx.description: Fraction of the target's width where the arrow attaches (0 left .. 1 right).

fy.description: Fraction of the target's height (0 top .. 1 bottom).

value.description: Required for Distance, Angle (radians), Radius, Diameter, DistanceX, DistanceY; forbidden otherwise. Scene units.

ref.description: Reference (measured, not driving). Dimensional kinds only.

groups.description: A group id needs at least two members; a lone id is removed on load.

frame.description: Id of a frame element that clips this one.

z.description: Fractional paint-order key within a layer, compared as plain strings; ties fall back to array order.

seed.description: Seeds the hand-drawn wobble; any integer.

name.description: User-visible name; must be unique among elements.

extras.description: Element keys the app does not interpret are kept as written. On the image with id "underlay" the key `underlay` holds its calibration (see $defs/underlayExtras). `provenance` marks an element an agent wrote (see $defs/provenance).

provenance.description: Who wrote the element and whether a person reviewed it (epic E8). Optional; a sheet without it keeps its exact bytes.

source.description: "agent" for anything written by sketch-cli edit.

confidence.description: Whole percent the agent reports; a belief, not a measurement.

accepted.description: True once a person accepted it in the editor; the marker stays.

sheetSetup.description: Optional print setup (epic E7), a sheet property read only by the exports: SVG/PNG/PDF on a page at a drawing scale. The drawing scale is not the view zoom: at 1:48 a 10 ft line (1920 scene units) is 2.5 inch on the paper. Absent until someone sets one, so a sheet that never did keeps its exact bytes. The title block, scale bar and north arrow are export furniture: not elements, not drawn in the editor.

paper.description: Letter, A4, A3, Tabloid, or a custom portrait size WxHmm / WxHin (for example 300x200mm, 8x10in). Default Letter.

margin.description: One length for every side. Default 0.5in (10mm on metric paper).

scale.description: Drawing scale as paper:real in lowest terms: 1:48 is 1/4 inch = 1 foot, 1:50 metric, 2:1 enlarges. Default 1:48.

scaleBar.description: Draw a scale bar, true to the drawing scale. Default true.

north.description: Degrees clockwise from up; absent draws no north arrow.

titleBlock.description: Absent draws no title block; notes adds a row.

underlayExtras.description: Optional. Marks the photo or plan underlay (epic E5): the image element with id "underlay" on the layer "underlay" (locked, below every other layer, layer opacity 0.5 by default). `px` is the photo's pixel size after EXIF orientation. `refs` are the known lengths it was scaled by: `a` and `b` are photo pixel coordinates (origin top-left, v down), `len` is the real distance in scene units (1/16 inch, a whole number). With refs the app and `sketch-cli` treat the photo as calibrated; one scale for the whole photo (no perspective correction). A sheet with no underlay carries none of this, so existing sheets keep their bytes.

angle.description: Radians, clockwise on screen, about the box centre.

rect.description: Rectangle. x,y is the top-left corner; the outline is stroked centred on the edge.

frame.description: Clipping frame; its title is `name`. Members point at it with `frame`.

ellipse.description: Centre and radii (not a box). rx == ry is a circle.

poly.description: true closes the shape back to the first point (and fills it with style.bg).

arrow.description: The points are absolute scene coordinates; bindings record which shapes the ends are attached to, they do not move the points.

text.description: As drawn, with \n between wrapped lines.

orig.description: The text before wrapping; defaults to `text`.

container.description: Id of a rect, diamond, ellipse or arrow this text labels.

lh.description: Line height as a multiple of the font size.

text.description: Drawn from the stored box, never re-measured: x,y,w,h must already fit the text (about 0.55 x fs per character wide, lh x fs per line tall).

fileId.description: Lowercase sha256 of the image bytes; the bytes live in the graph's asset store. The CLI draws a dashed placeholder.

pts.description: The drawn centreline; no two consecutive points may coincide (a closed wall also joins the last point back to the first). A closed wall needs at least 3 points.

t.description: Thickness in scene units (1 unit = 1/16 inch); 72 is 4 1/2 inches.

just.description: Where the body sits relative to the drawn line. Inside: the line is the room-side face, the body grows outward. Outside: the line is the outer face. Inside is the polygon interior of a closed wall, or the left of travel of an open one (y grows downward).

closed.description: true is a room: the last point joins back to the first.

wall.description: A wall drawn as a double line with mitred joints (a joint sharper than a 3:1 mitre is bevelled). The wall's style: `stroke`/`sw` draw the faces, `bg` fills the body. Openings that name this wall as their host cut the body.

host.description: Id of the wall element this opening sits on. An opening whose host is missing or is not a wall is kept but draws nothing; `validate` reports it.

seg.description: Index of the wall segment (the segment from point `seg` to the next point).

off.description: Distance in scene units from that segment's start point to the opening's start, along the centreline.

w.description: Width along the wall. Moved and narrowed on load so the opening lies inside the free span of the segment (between the joint mitres).

kind.description: A door cuts the body and draws a leaf with a swing arc, a window leaves the body and draws a frame with a pane line, an opening only cuts the body.

flipSide.description: false swings a door to the left of the wall's direction of travel, true to the right.

flipHinge.description: false hinges at the segment-start jamb, true at the far jamb.

x.description: Derived footprint (top-left of the unrotated box), rewritten from the host on every load and edit; omit when writing by hand.

h.description: Derived footprint height: the wall thickness.

angle.description: Derived footprint angle: the segment direction in radians.

a0.description: Start angle in radians; the arc sweeps toward increasing angle, which is clockwise on screen because y points down.
